title: readLock collapses a stat error into absent, so a break file it cannot stat is reported as nonexistent and the lock-removal advice becomes unsafe (QCLI-522 round-2 findings, N2 ranked first)
description:
Findings from the QCLI-522 round-2 FULL review (unit quest-cli-review-657r2, model deepseek-flash, DEC-183 Stage 1), which APPROVED opum-ai/quest-cli#657 at 75506c3a (merged as 38ba9fc5). ITEMS ARE IN RANK ORDER.

N2 (MINOR, first): src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts:308-309 is `stat(...).catch(() => null)`, which collapses EACCES, EIO and ELOOP into "absent". An unreadable break file then produces a false "No break file exists at ..." -- and since that is the branch that makes removing the lock sound safe, an operator is told the lock can be removed while a live breaker may hold an unreadable break file. Fix: narrow the catch to ENOENT; any other stat error must report the file PRESENT with an unknown age, using the existing "its age could not be read" wording. Correct readLock docblock at :298-300 to match.

N1 (MINOR): the new ENOENT read branch (:314-320) has no test. Add a seam and a case where stat succeeds and readFile throws ENOENT, asserting the hint says no break file exists.

N4 (NIT): breakFileStampedMillisecondsAgo is mtime-derived when the file is zero-byte. Rename it or document that, and pin the semantics in a test.

N5 (NIT): the CHANGELOG says the hint never gives a cause, while the hint itself names a hedged possibility. Reword so the two agree.

N6 (NIT): the dead-pid advice "Remove <break file> first" should add "if it still names pid N", because pid reuse can make that file another process.

N7 (NIT): the path assertions in the hint tests are still toContain, so a path that is a substring of the reported one passes. Assert the exact clause.

N8 (NIT): the unreadable end-to-end fixture cannot tell which of the two unreadable branches ran. Make it distinguish them.

Not to be worked until the day plan names it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The stat catch in readLock is narrowed to ENOENT: any other stat failure reports the break file as PRESENT with an unreadable age using the existing age-could-not-be-read wording, never as absent, and the readLock docblock describes the split
A test drives the seam where stat succeeds and readFile fails with ENOENT, asserting the hint reports that no break file exists
The mtime-derived stamp field is renamed or documented so its meaning is explicit for a zero-byte break file, and a test pins that semantics

The CHANGELOG no longer claims the hint never names a cause, the dead-pid advice is conditional on the file still naming that pid, the path assertions compare the exact clause rather than a substring, and the unreadable end-to-end fixture distinguishes which unreadable branch ran
